headline: Cloudflare Lets Websites Set Different Rules for AI Search, Agent, and Training Bots
what_happened: Cloudflare launched controls letting website owners set separate policies for three categories of AI bot traffic -- Search, Agent, and Training -- instead of one all-or-nothing block, choosing to allow or block each category and set a content-use level (no storage, reference-only, or full reuse) via a robots.txt extension.
why_it_matters: Cloudflare sits in front of more than 20% of the web, so its defaults effectively shape how AI crawlers can access much of the internet -- a concrete move in the fight over whether AI companies must pay for, or get, the content their models train on.
one_liner: Cloudflare now lets website owners decide separately whether AI search tools, AI agents, and AI model training can each access their site, instead of one all-or-nothing switch.

citations.quote: Being honest about what you do earns you more access, not less
